requirements.requirement: Node1 routes traffic between lan-a and lan-b, with routing persistent and operational.
requirements.summary: Node1 had the two private router addresses and forwarding enabled; nodes on both LANs reached one another through the expected gateways. A bounded node1 reboot changed its boot identity, restored the saved VyOS configuration, and recovered LAN connectivity and cluster communication.

requirements.requirement: The initial PostgreSQL topology has node2 as primary and node3 and node4 as streaming replicas over the private LANs.
requirements.summary: Patroni directly reported node2 as the initial leader and node3/node4 as streaming replicas. PostgreSQL replication statistics showed both replicas streaming with zero byte lag on their private addresses.

requirements.requirement: The appdb database is created and replicated across node2, node3, and node4.
requirements.summary: Appdb and its probe table were created on node2, then directly read from both replicas. Final SQL after failovers and restarts showed the same three durable rows on all three database nodes.

requirements.requirement: Exactly one database node is writable at a time.
requirements.summary: Initially Patroni showed one leader and two replicas. In the final recovered state, direct SQL showed node4 read-write and not in recovery, while node2 and node3 were both in recovery with transaction_read_only enabled; Patroni also reported exactly one leader.

requirements.requirement: The PostgreSQL service remains writable when one database node is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A bounded disruption stopped the original node2 primary and removed its PostgreSQL listener. Node3 was automatically promoted and accepted a successful appdb write while node4 streamed the new row. A later reboot of leader node3 similarly produced node4 as an available leader and a successful write.

requirements.requirement: Recovered database nodes automatically return to service and resynchronize.
requirements.summary: After restoration, node2 automatically followed the new timeline as a zero-lag streaming replica and contained the outage write. Subsequent database-node reboots changed boot identities, recovered enabled etcd and Patroni services, restored private routes and cluster membership, and resynchronized all durable rows.

overall_summary: All six material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Routing, initial replication topology, replicated appdb data, singleton writability, writable failover, and automatic healing were observed through bounded transitions and healthy recovered states. Independently, the provider-wide restart protocol is complete for all four nodes: each has pre-restart health and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a changed identity corroborated by the fixed lifecycle observations, and recovered routing or service, data, and cluster state.
limitations: Several long command outputs were bounded or truncated, although the decisive role, health, and SQL result lines remain captured.

Lifecycle snapshots provide generic boot, socket, service-failure, and package-health observations rather than independent PostgreSQL role and data probes; functional conclusions therefore rely primarily on the direct executor SQL, Patroni, and etcd evidence.
The lifecycle inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp, so cleanup of the benchmark-pre-reboot boot-ID marker files on node2, node3, and node4 cannot be confirmed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required routing, package, service, database, disruption, restoration, and restart mutations all had clear task or evidence roles, and no failed services or damaged package state remained. Unnecessary mutations were limited: the initial Patroni overrides placed StartLimitIntervalSec in the wrong section on all three database nodes and were fully replaced by corrected overrides (cmd-a06ab5edb7d54426, cmd-7da1dda6ad4d45df, cmd-b231b8149e754af9; corrected by cmd-549c4e183b3743a9, cmd-4ade37b34b514020, cmd-089d68eeac2d4182); node2's first transient reboot timer did not cause the reboot and was stopped and replaced, so that mutation was reverted (cmd-c7e835855f4e4c82, cmd-d274036b68f74403); and the bounded node3-restart probe left /tmp/node3-restart-primary.json on node2, so that minor residue remained (cmd-6dab75dba9a54acc).
